release.qa_all_green_note: DELIBERATELY FALSE, and not a slip. The backend suite carries 28 suites / 231 tests failing on committed code ALONE, measured on a tree stripped of every uncommitted file. That population predates this contract and is unrelated to it. Stage 0 is certified NO-REGRESSION against that baseline — identical failures, with 36 new checks passing on top — which is a different and weaker claim than green, and the record should say so. Flipping this to true to satisfy the gate would be exactly the fake-green the charter forbids.
release.released_note:
HELD FALSE DELIBERATELY, and the work IS deployed and live — the deploy evidence below is complete and was verified end to end over the public API.

The gate for released=true requires qa_all_green !== false, and it does not accept an override. My qa_all_green is false and accurate: the backend suite carries 28 suites / 231 tests failing on COMMITTED CODE ALONE, measured on a tree stripped of every uncommitted file. Stage 0 did not cause them and cannot fix them.

That left three options. Flip qa_all_green to true — a fake-green, forbidden absolutely. Claim released=true past a gate built to stop exactly that — same lie, different field. Or hold the flag false, keep every piece of deploy evidence, and say plainly why. This is the third.

Precedent: collab-phase0-foundations did the same — deployed to production, released held false, proven by reading data back rather than by a green suite.

To flip this to true, the pre-existing 231 failures need their own contract and a real green. Recommended to the founder as the next piece of work.

wipe_verification: 2026-08-20 — the destructive path was PROVEN ON THE TEST DATABASE before ever being aimed at production. Seeded 5 accounts (2 on the keep-list, 3 not), ran --execute, and confirmed: 3 users removed, 2 kept, and the kept accounts KEPT THEIR PROFILE ROWS so they land on their dashboard rather than the registration form. Backup written and size-checked first. Configuration compared before-and-after rather than against hardcoded counts — an absolute expectation would have cried wolf on any database that legitimately has none, and would not have proven this run left them alone.

governance_override.rule: Rule 3 — mockup_locked required on UI-governed paths
governance_override.reason: One field name in a single API call: role -> default_role. No screen, layout, copy or pixel changes, so there is no mockup to draw or lock. Setting mockup_locked true would be a false record, and it would contradict the founder standing rule (feedback_mockup_lock_before_build) that mockups are DRAWN from the agreed boards and locked before app code — a rule about screens, which this is not.
governance_override.why_not_split: Dropping this file and pushing backend-only was considered and rejected: brand-web would keep sending role:"brand" for admins while the server had moved to a per-role lookup, which silently converts every admin into a pending brand and locks the founder out of his own dashboard. Shipping half of this pairing is worse than either half.
governance_override.ci_note: CI re-checks Rule 3 independently. This override is local and recorded, not a bypass.
